messages:
mark: Quick questionI had to extend my hotel stay in Prague because my visa appointment ran late and I couldn't fly out the same day. Company paid for conference nights (Sept 10-12) but I extended to the 13th on my personal card. Can I expense the extra night and meals under "emergency travel"? cc @priya

priya: Sorry that happened. Short answer: we cover reasonable incremental costs caused by mandatory work-related delays (visa/consulate issues) if you can show proof. You'll need receipts and a short explanation of why it was unavoidable.

mark: Proof: the consulate email shows the appointment was rescheduled to the afternoon and the earliest flight home was the next day. Hotel was 85, dinner 18, train 12. I paid all personally.

jen: Workflow: create one travel expense for the business nights and a separate incident expense called "visa-delay-2026-09-12". Attach consulate email, full hotel folio, train ticket and meal receipt. Add note: "consulate reschedule prevented same-day travel" and tag project `INTL-OPS`.

expense-bot: Policy snippet: "Unplanned, work-related travel interruptions (visa delays, mandatory appointments) are eligible for reimbursement of incremental lodging, meals, and necessary local transport when documented. Manager approval required for incident claims."

priya: A couple of tips: 1) If the hotel folio combines nights, request an itemized nightly breakdown from the property; if unavailable, include a manager-signed attestation. 2) For meals where partner joined, claim only your portion and annotate the receipt.

mark: Got it. One more: the consulate charged a mandatory service fee printed on a separate receipt. Is that reimbursable?

jen: Mandatory government or consulate fees required for work travel (e.g., visa fees) are reimbursable. Upload the official receipt and include the rationale in the expense note.

mark: Thanks all, uploading now. Appreciate the fast help :thumbsup:
